channel.title: EU & Swiss News Feed
channel.description: Latest news from Europe covering politics, economy, and security

item.title: [DW] Wael Mohya could make German football history at 17
item.description: At just 17, Gladbach forward Wael Mohya has earned his first Germany call-up. The dual-national talent has chosen the DFB path for now — and could soon make modern national-team history.

item.title: [DW] British counterterrorism police arrest US soldier accused of spying on behalf of Russia
item.description: A member of the US Army has been arrested near Gloucester in England. Police said he was suspected of espionage activity in connection with Russia. Investigators from the US and UK are involved in the probe.

item.title: [DW] UK Privy Council overrules Trinidad and Tobago gay sex law
item.description: A London court has overturned a Trinidad and Tobago law criminalizing consensual sexual relations between male same-sex couples. As a result of the colonial legacy, it is the independent country's last court of appeal.

item.title: [DW] Victims of Nazi war in Poland call on Germany for support
item.description: More than 80 years after the end of World War II, Polish victims of the Nazi regime are still waiting for a "humanitarian gesture" from Germany. The 2027 draft budget hasn't left them much hope for possible reparations.

item.title: [DW] EU leaders tussle over whom to send to Ukraine, Russia peace talks
item.description: A seat at the table for Europe now appears likely following comments by a US envoy who just held talks with Putin. But who will take that seat remains unclear.

item.title: [DW] Can the EU make it harder to trick consumers online?
item.description: The EU wants to curb subscription traps, misleading sales tactics and features that keep people scrolling. What would the proposed Digital Fairness Act change, and does it go far enough?

item.title: [DW] What have the talks with Russia and the US in Abu Dhabi achieved for Ukraine?
item.description: The first trilateral talks between Ukraine, the US and Russia in nine months have ended with an agreement on exchanging prisoners. Does this mark a genuine breakthrough and a step toward peace?

item.title: [DW] Hungary eases abortion restrictions in women's rights overhaul
item.description: The reforms mark a break the the conservative policies of former PM Viktor Orban. The controversial "heartbeat regulation" is to be scrapped and women are to be better protected against violence.

item.title: [DW] UK court convicts 2 Iranian men of spying on journalists
item.description: A London court has found two Iranian citizens guilty of surveilling reporters for a Persian-language television station critical of Iran's government. One was also convicted of planning a violent attack against them.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU flexes muscle on Russia sanctions, as Trump and Putin discuss Ukraine’s future in China
item.description: If new EU sanctions on Russia were meant to show strength at a delicate moment in Ukraine peace talks, they could have been stronger.

item.title: [DW] Despite restrictive abortion laws, Poland's 'Abortomat' — a locker that dispenses abortion pills — helps women who want to end a pregnancy
item.description: Abortion laws in Poland are very restrictive. Activists there have found a new way to help women wanting to terminate a pregnancy: the "Abortomat," a locker that dispenses abortion pills. But they face fierce opposition.

item.title: [EU Observer] ‘Not apathy but disconnection’: We asked Europe’s youngest MEPs what they thought of the continent-wide Gen Z protests
item.description: From Porto to Athens, Europe was taken by surprise by the mass youth protests for better education, an affordable cost of living, and political accountability. EUobserver spoke to 12 of the youngest MEPs in the European Parliament to understand the issues at the heart of Gen Z unrest.

item.title: [DW] Ukraine: Zelenskyy says security deal could go to referendum
item.description: The US has broached the idea of Kyiv giving up the Donbas region in exchange for NATO membership, the Ukrainian president said.

item.title: [EU Observer] Nuclear weapons – the elephant in the room in Ukraine peace talks
item.description: Since February 2022, president Vladimir Putin has used tacit and overt nuclear threats to try to achieve tactical advantage in the full-scale invasion of Ukraine. And now there are no guardrails. For almost a year, the United States and Russia have had no binding limits on their strategic arsenals.

item.title: [DW] Turkey uses espionage accusations to pressure government critics
item.description: The arrest of a German foundation's employee in Istanbul this week has put the focus back on pressure tactics used by the Erdogan administration. The arrest is far from the first of its kind.

item.title: [DW] Gen Z protests: Do Baby Boomers really have it better than young people?
item.description: Should young people in Germany be more worried about their future than Baby Boomers were in the 1980s and 1990s? Or should both generations take to the streets and protest together? DW checked the data.

item.title: [Politico Europe] French presidential rivals take aim at Le Pen in debate
item.description: The far-right leader and four other candidates were quizzed on cost-of-living issues.

item.description: Thursday’s unprecedented meeting of Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin has drawn intense international attention

item.description: The British prime minister said Brexit was "the first domino to fall in a global move towards isolationism and protectionism."

item.description: Boris Johnson's 'oven ready' Brexit deal never tasted very good. That's part of the 'obvious truth' about Brexit, according to UK PM Andy Burnham.

item.description: L’Union des clubs européens estime que l’accord d’exclusivité conclu entre l’UEFA et une puissante organisation de clubs de football enfreint le droit européen de la concurrence.

item.title: [EU Observer] Ukraine damages Crimean Bridge, drones likely hit arch (Ukraine Battlefield update, Day 1,726)
item.description: Ukrainian drones pound the Crimean Bridge and Russian tanks stall in fog near Dobropillia. In the meantime, commanders on both sides are gambling lives and prestige on offensives that keep collapsing under precision strikes.

item.title: [Politico Europe] UK hands Palantir two-year reprieve on NHS contract
item.description: Health minister James Frith described the extension of Palantir's NHS contract as “a bridge, not the destination.”

item.title: [Politico Europe] Le bras de fer entre Le Pen et les constitutionnalistes
item.description: L’initiative n’est pas habituelle : 110 professeurs de droit ont cosigné une tribune dans Le Monde, mercredi dernier, pour rappeler les règles prévues en matière révision de la Constitution. Leur message : modifier notre loi fondamentale via l’article 11, utilisé jadis par Charles de Gaulle, est irrégulier. Or, Marine Le Pen prévoit d’y recourir pour […]

item.title: [EU Observer] Europe’s mandate on Russia-Ukraine peace talks takes shape, as Putin escalates war
item.description: While Europe crafts its role in the Ukraine peace talks, Vladimir Putin’s renewed offensive raises the cost of every EU decision.

item.title: [EU Observer] Five EU countries tout Rwanda deportation partnership, but no formal deal as key details remain secret
item.description: Rwanda is set to host a so-called EU return hub. No formal deal has been announced as technical details still need to be sorted out in negotiations. The hope is to start deporting people next year.

item.title: [EU Observer] More EU sanctions on Russian propagandists and hackers, as thousands of fake accounts target voters
item.description: The EU agreed on Monday (16 November) to sanction 30 people and two organisations over Russian cyberattacks and disinformation campaigns targeting Europe, as researchers uncovered thousands of fake accounts used to target election campaigns.

item.description: Founder of country’s largest online retailer Wildberries targeted in latest round of EU sanctions over war in Ukraine

item.description: Austria, Denmark, Germany, Greece and the Netherlands plan to open the deportation hubs in 2027.

item.title: [EU Observer] [Interview] ‘Georgia has reached final stage of autocratic consolidation,’ warns former deputy foreign minister
item.description: Georgia’s fall from EU frontrunner to near-total state capture is not just a regional tragedy but a case study in how Russia exploits European complacency to pull an entire country back into its orbit, explains former minister.

item.title: [Euractiv] The Industrial Accelerator Act Cannot Overlook Finished Products [Promoted Content]
item.description: Written by Adam McCarthy. Every plane that lands, each tractor working a field and every ambulance rushing to a patient depends on tyres. Yet EU industrial policy tends to focus on raw materials and technologies, with less attention to finished strategic energy-intensive products such as tyres which keep the economy moving and essential services functioning. […]

item.title: [Politico Europe] SPONSORED EPISODE: Europe’s ambition to stop cancer
item.description: Europe is a leader in cancer research. But turning that science into treatments that reach patients is another matter. Every minute, five people in Europe are diagnosed with cancer, and the disease costs the European economy more than €100 billion a year. Five years after its launch, Europe’s Beating Cancer Plan has been scrutinized by […]

item.title: [EU Observer] What Marine Le Pen and Alice Weidel are planning for Brussels
item.description: The AfD's Alice Weidel envisages reducing EU powers under existing rules within three years, pursuing treaty reform within seven, and using Germany's budgetary leverage along the way. Hot on her heels, Marine Le Pen is looking towards national elections across Europe to build a coalition of like-minded governments.

item.title: [Euractiv] Organic farmers warn of substantial support cuts in next CAP
item.description: MEPs are debating their position on the issue this week

item.title: [EU Observer] ‘Prague doesn’t want Nazis’: Activists block Slovak far-right MEP from conference about deporting immigrants
item.description: In a heavily guarded Prague hotel, anti-migrant ideologues from Germany, Hungary and Czech Republic rallied together in support of a petition to deport foreigners that was rejected by the EU on rights grounds. MEP Milan Mazurek, previously convicted of inciting hatred towards Roma, was stopped from going inside by antifascist protesters.

item.description: Rapporteur's draft report also pushes for environmental carve-outs

item.title: [EU Observer] EU Commission clears UniCredit’s Commerzbank takeover, tells Berlin not to stand in the way
item.description: The European Commission has waved through Europe’s biggest cross-border bank takeover since the financial crisis, and warned it would “react accordingly” to any national government trying to block it.

item.title: [Euractiv] Why Europe should move to proactive respiratory care [Promoted Content]
item.description: Europe can improve COPD outcomes through earlier identification, timely care and coordination across primary, specialist and community settings. Responsible innovation can reduce disease worsening and hospitalizations while supporting sustainable healthcare and protecting patient choice, continuity of care and equitable access.

item.description: History’s warning from Yalta hangs over today’s secretive talks, as European leaders answer an existential carve‑up threat with a clumsy committee instead of a single hard‑nosed envoy who knows the Kremlin’s playbook.

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: Is Europe ready to defend itself against cyberattacks?
item.description: Bomb threats, election interference, espionage, and sabotage. Cyberattacks are becoming an increasingly serious threat across Europe, affecting everything from public services to critical infrastructure. So, how prepared is Europe to deal with them?

item.title: [EU Observer] THIS WEEK: EU piles on more Russia sanctions, a crunch UK-EU summit, and budget wrangles
item.description: The draft new sanctions list includes Russia's richest woman, Tatyana Kim, as well as dozens of Russian banks and propagandists, with both France and Germany saying that the extra sanctions were already a done deal.

item.description: And may soon have to pay the price for its obsession

item.title: [DW] The dangers of revising Europe's security architecture
item.description: Experts warn against revising Europe's security framework because they say it would mean granting Moscow its longstanding wish of renegotiating postwar security on the continent.

item.title: [DW] Czechia braces for massive protest against public media reform plans
item.description: A fast-tracked bill to cut public media funding has sparked strikes, rallies and fears for the independence of public broadcasting in Czechia. A massive protest is planned for Prague on Sunday.
